newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain to prosecute leaders of ETA political arm.
newsitem.headline: Spain to prosecute leaders of ETA political arm.

text.p: Spain's Supreme Court has summoned the leaders of the political arm of the Basque separatist ETA guerrilla organisation to answer charges that they promoted violence, according to court documents issued on Friday.
The decision by Supreme Court Judge Jose Manuel Martinez to call all 25 executive members of the Herri Batasuna (HB) party lifts their political immunity to prosecution.
They will be charged with editing and distributing an ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) videotape during the campaign for a general election last March.

The video, which was played in Basque bars, clubs and schools at the start of the campaign, depicts hooded, armed rebels pleading their case. ETA has killed some 800 people since 1968 in its drive for Basque independence.

The HB leaders will also be charged over two statements justifying the assassinations last February of former judge Francisco Tomas y Valiente and lawyer Fernando Mugica, as well as over an internal party document.

The two murders sparked widespread debate in the country over whether ETA's political arm should be outlawed and the then-ruling Socialist government said it would start legal proceedings against HB leaders.
A high court judge had since decided to take action against the party leaders, but he needed to appeal to the Supreme Court to get their immunity lifted.
Basque Socialist party spokesman Fernando Buesa greeted the Supreme Court order "with satisfaction".
"It is not permissible that the directors of HB seek protection in the name of democracy in order to coloborate with ETA and apologise for terrorism," he said in a statement.
A Socialist party centre in the Basque region was set on fire on Friday by a group of hooded attackers believed to one of several violent youth groups that support ETA.

The building in the northern city of Hernani, a hotbed of support for the militant group, was damaged in the attack and a 48-year-old man was taken to hospital for smoke inhalation, although police said he was not seriously injured.

Spanish police have made several arrests of members of the youth groups in recent weeks, leading Interior Minister Jaime Mayor Oreja to warn early this week that ETA could be planning an attack in retaliation.

A Spanish army officer was shot and killed in Madrid on Wednesday in an apparent ETA attack only hours after an HB spokesman said Mayor Oreja was "playing with fire" and warned that there would be "great suffering in the immediate future".
The attorney general said on Thursday that he was studying possible court action against HB for the statement.

Herri Batasuna has seen its vote fall steadily since 1987, but it still won two parliamentary seats in the general election, getting popular support from small, usually poor areas in the north coast provinces of Guipuzcoa and Vizcaya.
